topics.topic: Definition, observation, and propagation of the upload arrival timestamp
questions: Which module captures the exact monotonic reading at which the upload head finishes, and how is that reading conveyed to `owner_sessions`, given that `upload_framing` owns completion of the head read, `owner_sessions` alone may read the clock, and neither may know the other under the dependency order?
Is an upload's arrival instant the instant the bounded head finishes being read, or the later instant when `operations` hands the request to `owner_sessions`?

Is an upload's arrival instant the instant its head finishes being read, or the later instant when `operations` hands it to `owner_sessions`; and which permitted module observes and timestamps that event, given that `owner_interface` no longer knows `clock`, `upload_framing` does not know `clock`, and `owner_sessions` cannot observe head completion?

quotes:
The
  limits of A13 are read by `owner_sessions` from `clock.monotonic_reading`,
  an owner request's arrival among them — for an upload, once its bounded
  head has been read (A13 rule 2);

the session's
validity at a request's arrival, read when `operations` hands the request to
the session check — for an upload after its head, at most
`UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES`, has been read (rule 2; owner, 2026-11-17);
judgement.why: The texts make the handoff to owner_sessions after the bounded head read the upload's arrival event, and owner_sessions itself takes the monotonic reading, so no timestamp is captured by or conveyed from upload_framing.

topics.topic: How upload bodies without a declared length are delimited and supported
questions: How does the request-body stream determine its end when the request declares no length, which A19 explicitly allows, and does `instance_lifecycle` support such an upload or refuse it?
How must `instance_lifecycle` delimit and hand on a body when the request declares no length, which A19 rule 4 explicitly permits for an upload?
How is the request-body stream delimited when the request declares no length, which A19 explicitly permits for an upload?

quotes:
The limit is counted
over the bytes Registry receives, never over a length the request
declares: a declared length over the limit is refused before any byte is
read; otherwise Registry reads the upload up to one byte more than the
limit and refuses it as soon as it holds more than the limit, whatever
length was declared or whether one was.
judgement.why: How an HTTP body without a declared length is framed, terminated, and represented is an encoding and contract question assigned to State 6, not a State 3 module-ownership question.

For every non-upload owner request, how much of its body may be read before `operations` hands it to the session check?
For a non-upload form, does `operations` hand the request to the session check after headers, after the CSRF/form fields have been parsed, or only after the complete body has been read?

quotes:
the session's
validity at a request's arrival, read when `operations` hands the request to

judgement.why: The point in request parsing and routing at which a non-upload request is handed to operations is flow ordering, which belongs to State 4 rather than State 3 ownership.

topics.topic: Whether malformed, incomplete, or over-bound upload heads reach session admission and refresh idle time
questions: When `read_upload_head` returns no CSRF value, must `owner_interface` still call `operations` so the owner-session check occurs and a valid session's idle time is restarted, or may the framing layer/interface refuse the request before admission?

Does “an upload” include a request to the upload route whose bounded head is malformed, exceeds the head bound, lacks the expected CSRF first part, or yields no file part; and if so, does that request refresh a valid session's idle limit?

What counts as the head having been read when the body ends early, the multipart head is malformed, or no complete head is found within the bound; does such a request reach the owner-session check and restart the idle period?

part, and the file part's declared length — the request's declared length

judgement.why: The later operation text sends every listed malformed, incomplete, or over-bound head onward with no CSRF value, refuses it at the session check, and states that a valid-session arrival restarts the idle period even when the answer is a CSRF refusal.

topics.topic: Atomic ordering of session admission, timestamp updates, expiry, and sign-out
questions: What is the atomic ordering among taking the arrival reading, acquiring the session lock, checking validity, updating the last-request reading, and an expiry pass removing the session?

How is a request that has passed the session check guaranteed to complete if the expiry pass or sign-out can take the session lock and remove the session before that request takes the lock; is admission atomic with acquiring or reserving the session?

quotes:
A request that passed
completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs or waits (A13
rule 2). After the check, a change that touches no uploaded file takes its
place on the session's lock at once; a request that touches one first waits
for the import lock and then takes its place, so the locks are always taken
import first and no place on a session's lock waits for the import lock (A16
rule 2). A request asks for the import lock when it is admitted. The import
lock is granted in the order requests asked for it, and
the session's lock in the order places were taken, and the session's
changes apply one at a time in that order (A13 rule 2: "in the order in
which they take the session's one lock").

The pass alone
ends sessions by their limits: it takes the import lock, reads
`clock.monotonic_reading` once, and decides every session by that one
reading, in the order of their sign-in, each under its own lock, so the
order decides nothing. Its turn on a session's lock comes after every change
of the session admitted before the pass began, which completes first with
the confirmation and the upload it may need (A13 rule 2).

From its admission the session is marked signed out, and no request of the
session arriving after it passes the check, a read included (State 4,
`flow:owner_sign_in_and_session`: a request arriving after the sign-out is
refused at the session check).
Its turn on the session's lock comes after every change of the session
admitted before it: one touching no uploaded file took its place at its
admission, before the sign-out, which takes its own only after the import
lock; one touching an uploaded file asked for the import lock before the
sign-out did, and that lock is granted in order (`admit_owner_request`).
Each completes first, its change to the store
included, with the confirmation and the upload it may need still in place,
and leaves nothing in the ended session.
judgement.why: The later session operations reserve the required lock order at admission and explicitly place expiry and sign-out after every previously admitted change, guaranteeing that an admitted request completes.

topics.topic: How a declared-length request body terminates when the client sends too few bytes
questions: What concrete rule makes the stream stop when a client declares more bytes than it sends before waiting for an answer: timeout, premature-end detection, cancellation, or immediate refusal?

When a client declares a body longer than the bytes it sends and waits for an answer without closing the connection, what concrete event ends or fails the stream so the stated non-waiting guarantee holds?

judgement.why: Timeouts, premature transport termination, cancellation, and the failure semantics of a request-body stream are operation and contract details assigned to State 6.

topics.topic: What transient state is permitted before upload admission
questions: Does “no state” mean no owner-session state, no authentication state, or literally no request/parser state, and what transient bounded head or multipart parser state is permitted before admission?

What state is forbidden between receipt of the headers and admission: owner-session state only, durable application state, or also the multipart parser's bounded buffer, delimiter look-ahead, body stream and connection state?
